transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just cannot keep my mind on one thing anymore. It's getting really bad. Like, I'll be working in the shop, and just one saw starting up, or somebody walking past the office... speaking of the office, we just got this new guy, Greg, and he wears these heavy work boots that just clomp so loud on the concrete. I told him he needs to get the ones with the softer soles, like the ones I wear. I've had this pair for, gosh, five years now? Best boots I ever bought. You just have to oil them every couple of months and they last forever, especially if you get the laces with the Kevlar in them... 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? 

Oh, right, my mind. Yeah, so Greg walks by, or even if I just have a random thought about another job we're contracted for, it just pulls me right off whatever I’m doing. And then I'm standing there holding a piece of trim, and the whole day just completely gets away from me.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling full of energy?

No, gosh no. I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get a solid seven or eight hours, I'm just dragging. Though honestly, I haven't been sleeping great lately anyway because of our mattress. I built the bed frame myself—solid cherry wood, beautiful mortise and tenon joints, took me a month of Sundays to get the finish exactly right. I used this natural tung oil blend... it really brings out the grain, you know? But the mattress we put on it is one of those foam ones that comes rolled up in a box, and my husband, Dave, he runs so hot at night, and that foam just traps all the heat. We were looking at getting one of those cooling pad things, but I went to the home goods store and completely forgot to check the measurements to see if our fitted sheets would still stretch over it, because they have those deep pockets now, but some of them aren't quite deep enough if you add a topper... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, energy. No, definitely not full of energy. I'm pretty wiped out most of the time, honestly.
Did you have these kinds of attention problems when you were a child?

Oh, yeah. Even way back in grade school, definitely before I was twelve. I remember my teachers were always telling my mother that I was a bright girl, but just so careless. I was always losing my homework, or I'd completely forget the instructions the second the teacher gave them. Mostly I was just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. 

Those old schools had these massive double-hung sash windows, you know? The ones with the heavy cast iron counterweights hidden inside the frames on thick cotton sash cords. I actually got hired to restore some windows just like that in a historic courthouse downtown a few years ago. You have to be so careful pulling the old stop molding off or it just splinters into a million pieces because the wood is a hundred years old and bone dry. We had to build this special steam box to loosen the old glazing putty, which smells absolutely terrible when it gets hot, kind of like rancid linseed oil... 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? 

Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, so I'd just stare out those big windows all day instead of doing my schoolwork. It's always been like this, I guess.
Have your thinking or memory problems gotten noticeably worse recently compared with how you’ve always been?

Well, worse... I mean, it's always been a struggle, but yeah, I'd say it's gotten a lot harder to manage lately. Really, it's been about a year and a month now. That's when I broke my wrist. Slipped on some ice loading up the truck—which, by the way, those tailgate latches on the newer models are just garbage. They use this cheap plastic housing instead of a solid steel catch, so when the temperature drops, the plastic gets brittle and just snaps. I ended up having to fabricate a replacement part out of some scrap aluminum I had in the shop just to get the tailgate to stay shut. Aluminum is great for that kind of thing because it won't rust, but you have to be careful when you're drilling it because it heats up so fast and can gum up your drill bit if you don't use a little cutting fluid... 

Wait, what did you ask me? 

Oh, right, my memory getting worse. Yeah, so since I broke my wrist, they shifted me off the hands-on carpentry and put me on shop paperwork and supervising. And sitting at a desk trying to keep track of invoices and schedules... it's just a nightmare. That's when I really noticed how bad it is.
When you slipped on the ice and broke your wrist, did you hit your head?

No, I didn't hit my head. Just went down hard on my right side and threw my hand out to catch myself. Classic mistake, really. You're supposed to tuck and roll, but instinct just takes over. I ended up with a Colles' fracture. The orthopedic guy was actually pretty impressed with the x-ray. Said it was a clean break, which made setting it a lot easier. 

I actually got to watch them put the fiberglass cast on. It's fascinating stuff, really. It's this woven fiberglass tape impregnated with a water-activated polyurethane resin. Once it gets wet, the chemical reaction starts and it hardens up in minutes. It's so much lighter than those old plaster of Paris casts they used to use. Plaster is basically just calcined gypsum—calcium sulfate hemihydrate—and when you mix it with water, it crystallizes back into gypsum. We use plaster all the time in restoration work for crown moldings and ceiling medallions. You have to work pretty fast before it sets, and you always end up with it all over your hands...

Sorry, I'm rambling again. No, I didn't hit my head at all. Just the wrist.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things?

Well, no, not really. I don't sit around worrying about everything under the sun. I mean, I worry about normal things, like if the lumber delivery is going to be late, because that throws off the whole schedule. And lumber prices right now, let me tell you, they are just all over the map. You try to bid a job, and by the time the client approves it, the cost of a sheet of three-quarter-inch birch plywood has jumped twenty percent. 

Birch is getting harder to find in good quality, anyway. A lot of the stuff coming in now has these terrible voids in the inner plies, so when you go to rip it on the table saw, the veneer just chips out along the cut line. It's infuriating. You can try scoring the cut line first with a marking knife, or using a zero-clearance insert on the saw, which definitely helps support the wood fibers. I actually made my own insert out of some scrap MDF... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, worrying. No, I don't really have a problem with worrying too much. Just the usual stuff.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern of inattentive and distractible behavior beginning before age 12, including losing homework, forgetting instructions, staring out the window, and current difficulty sustaining focus, being pulled off task by external stimuli and internal thoughts, and losing track of the conversation. Symptoms cause functional impairment, especially after reassignment to paperwork and scheduling duties. Mania is not supported (no decreased need for sleep or increased energy), generalized anxiety is denied, and head injury was denied, reducing concern for secondary cognitive causes.
